Inca Cueva is an archaeological complex in the highlands of Jujuy Province. Its rock shelters lie within a gorge surrounded by red sandstone and the dry landscapes of the Puna. Rock paintings from different periods survive on the walls, while archaeological discoveries reveal the history of people who lived in northern Argentina over many thousands of years.

The site's name refers to the Incas, although the complex's history began long before they arrived in the region. Today specialists study and preserve the paintings, including those in caves 1 and 4. At Inca Cueva, the ancient art is experienced alongside the surrounding gorge, its rock overhangs and the open high-altitude landscape.

Inhotim in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais combines an open-air contemporary art museum with a botanical garden. Exhibition pavilions stand amid tropical greenery, gardens and lakes.

Here, encounters with works of art alternate with walks through the grounds. Visitors move on foot between the pavilions through gardens and areas of forest, so it is worth setting aside a dedicated part of the day for a visit.

Inhotim features on itineraries through Minas Gerais alongside Ouro Preto and Belo Horizonte. After the colonial architecture and historic towns, it offers an introduction to contemporary Brazilian art.

The museum is often included on excursions from Quito together with the historic center and the Middle of the World monument.
